creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A board with three enum fields worth seeing can only show two of them. `type_indicator` and `tint` each take one enum; `badges` takes `enum-set`, `free-set` and `boolean` but not `enum`, so the third field drops to the card detail view.

Hit on the spool board, which has `type`, `provenance` and `effort`. Putting `provenance` in badges gives:

    ! [INVALID_CARD_DISPLAY] main card_display.badges should reference set or
      boolean fields (enum-set, free-set, or boolean), but 'provenance' is
      type 'enum'

The workaround is to declare the field `enum-set` instead, which is wrong - it lets a card carry two provenances, and it changes how `--sort` ranks a card (highest-ranked value rather than the one value).

An enum in `badges` has an obvious rendering: one chip, the option's color, the same as an enum-set carrying exactly one value. `boolean` is already allowed there and is not a set either, so the slot is not strictly set-only today.

Where: `card_display.badges` validation, and whatever `kan doctor`'s INVALID_CARD_DISPLAY check reads.
title: card_display badges rejects enum, so only two enum fields fit on a card face
